transcript:
Meeting header
Date/Time: 2026-09-28 15:00 PT
Duration: ~42 minutes
Recording: cloud
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Daniel Kim (Redwood SE), Priya Rao (Atlas Platform), Liam O'Connor (Atlas SRE), Sara Mendes (Atlas ML), Jordan Price (Product)

Summary: quick handoff from discovery to POC scoping focused on latency SLOs (TTFT vs TPOT), sampling strategy for p95/p99, and runbook for benchmark measurement. Agreed to run Redwood harness against Atlas staging for baseline and one dedicated capacity check.

Topics: SLO defs, sampling size, traffic shaping, tail behavior, measurement windows, acceptance thresholds, security checkpoint, timeline for pilot kickoff.

Transcript body:
[00:00] Maya (Redwood): hey everyone thanks for joining, we wanted to use this time to turn the discovery notes into something we can actually run — outline SLOs and the sampling plan. hope that's ok.
[00:09] Priya (Atlas): yeah that's perfect, we had a few internal questions on TTFT importance vs per token cost, and also what exact p95/p99 we're measuring.
[00:18] Daniel (Redwood): good, we'll go through the definitions quickly — when i say TTFT i mean time to first token from request arrival, that's client-facing latency. TPOT or T-P-O-T in docs is total per token time — basically per token processing accounting across the response. we usually measure p50/p95/p99 for both but they have different significance.
[00:36] Sara (Atlas): oh yeah we call TTFT first byte in our infra, sometimes it's FBT, so just making sure mapping is clear. also our product cares about TTFT for interactive flows, but for batch generation TPOT throughput matters.
[00:50] Liam (Atlas): quick constraint from SRE side: our staging GPUs are A10s and we will want to compare hosted to a dedicated pool assumption, so please show what the harness will run.
[00:59] Daniel: noted. we'll parameterize device type. for this POC we recommend two main benchmark axes: 1) TTFT under low concurrency (1-8 concurrent requests) with varied prompt lengths, 2) TPOT throughput sweep (batched inference up to the target qps) to find p95 tail at target load.
[01:20] Jordan (Atlas): how many samples do we need to get a stable p99 estimate? those tails are costly.
[01:26] Daniel: great question — recommended sample sizes: for p95 1k requests per test bucket is usually enough; for p99 we target at least 10k effective samples. because p99 is tail-heavy we also suggest bootstrapping across 3 runs and using the merged distribution. we'll also capture server-side traces.
[01:45] Priya: okay that sounds large but feasible. do you recommend synthetic warmup or using a production replay trace?
[01:53] Maya: use both — replay for representative tails and synthetic for controlled sweep (length, concurrency). the replay will surface prefix/K V cache benefits or misses — note that transcription sometimes writes KV as K V cache.
[02:08] Sara: kv cache yes, we rely on cache hit rates to reduce TTFT for conversational flows. if the harness can't reproduce cache locality we may undercount improvements.
[02:18] Daniel: we'll include a 'sessionized' traffic mode in the harness to mimic KV reuse and a fully-shuffled mode to emulate cold-start behavior.
[02:27] Liam: what about measurement windows and system jitter? we want to avoid measuring during autoscaler eviction windows.
[02:33] Daniel: we'll run steady-state windows: 5 minute warmup, 10 minute measurement window, 5 minute cool down per sweep point. if you want to be stricter we can extend to 15 minute measurement windows.
[02:46] Priya: and the SLO targets — what are you proposing as acceptance criteria?
[02:50] Maya: from the discovery we captured your product targets: interactive features aim for TTFT p95 < 250ms and p99 < 500ms on 99% of production-like requests, whereas background generators are fine with TPOT p95 < 120ms per token at our target batch size. but those are starting points — we should align on sample buckets (short/mid/long prompts).
[03:12] Jordan: short/mid/long buckets = prompt tokens < 64, 64-512, 512+?
[03:17] Daniel: yes that's consistent, though for some models long prompts might be 1024+. we'll map to your observed distribution.
[03:23] Sara: do you recommend p99 be the gating metric or p95?
[03:27] Maya: depends on use-case: for user-facing chat p99 is important for UX, but many teams roll on p95 + p99 monitoring for regressions. for POC acceptance we usually require p95 to meet target and p99 to be within a reasonable tail budget (e.g., not more than 2x p95). we'll capture both.
[03:45] Liam: ok so acceptance rule: p95 meet target AND p99 <= 2x p95 (or absolute cap 1s) — that fits our SRE risk posture.
[03:55] Daniel: noted and we'll reflect in the measurement report. also call out the difference between client perceived latency (TTFT) and billed per-token latency; our logs will show both client side and server side.
[04:08] Maya: on the dedicated vs hosted question — for the POC we can run a hosted baseline and then a small dedicated pool to compare. Atlas mentioned wanting capacity isolation later.
[04:18] Priya: yes please show both, and include data residency notes — our compliance team will want to see logs retention and KMS usage.
[04:26] Olivia (Redwood CSM): we will attach SOC2 + KMS integration doc in the follow-up.
[04:31] Jordan: are you going to measure cost per 1k tokens at target throughput too? we need cost-economics.
[04:36] Maya: yes cost-per-token at each sweep point is part of the deliverable — we also provide a sensitivity chart for batching and quantization.
[04:44] Priya: quantization — our models may need fp16 vs int8 tradeoffs, will that be part of the run?
[04:50] Daniel: we can include a quantization axis if you want, but it's heavier because model conversion and accuracy checks are needed. for the first pass we recommend default precision used in your prod model, and optionally run an int8 sweep on a copy.
[05:03] Sara: accuracy/regression checks — we need to ensure response quality doesn't degrade when we change quant or batching.
[05:09] Daniel: harness will capture a small eval set (we ask you to provide 200 prompts) and compute basic similarity metrics and a checklist of high-risk prompts.
[05:20] Liam: traffic shaping — we have bursty weekend traffic, is it ok to test with a traffic spike profile?
[05:26] Daniel: yes we have a spike test to simulate burst and observe autoscaler/fallback behavior. for fallback policies we can show how Redwood routes to a cheaper/compatible model variant under heavy load, but that requires pre-approved variants.
[05:40] John (misattributed): [laughs] — uh speaker tags are occasionally wrong in these transcripts, ignore.
[05:45] Maya: good point, real transcript may have small mislabels.
[05:48] Jordan: timeline wise, what's realistic?
[05:52] Maya: quick timeline proposal: you send traffic CSV and eval set by 2026-09-30; Redwood shares harness and runbook by 2026-10-01; sample run and baseline (hosted) by 2026-10-04; review results and agree dedicated run on 2026-10-06 kickoff.
[06:10] Priya: that seems fast but doable. we'll confirm internal reviewers for security.
[06:16] Sara: what about p99 sample size cost? we might not want to run 10k samples for every bucket. can we prioritize short and mid buckets?
[06:25] Daniel: yes prioritize short and mid for full p99; for long prompts we can do approximate tails with focused replay of heavy-tail traces.
[06:33] Liam: one more SRE ask — leak metrics and memory growth traces, we need to sign off on OOM risk.
[06:40] Daniel: harness collects GPU mem usage, per-process RSS and GC metrics where available. we'll flag any growth trends.
[06:48] Maya: ok next steps recap — runbook, traffic CSV, schedule kickoff. any blockers on the Atlas side?
[06:55] Priya: security review is the only one — SOC2 doc and KMS notes should unblock.
[07:01] Olivia: we'll attach the security packet and a checklist for the auditor.
[07:05] Jordan: final question — what happens if p95 passes but p99 doesn't? is that an automatic fail?
[07:10] Maya: no it's contextual — we surface adaptive mitigations (batching changes, model variants, cache priming) and propose remediation steps. for POC acceptance we want p95 passing and a documented remediation plan for p99.
[07:23] Sara: sounds fair.
[07:25] Maya: thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the harness link and the schedule.
[07:29] Priya: thanks all.

End of meeting.
